This vignette collects the problems users run into most often, with their causes and fixes. Most of
them involve Python, because many rml classes run Python code through the reticulate package.

## Python

### Which classes need Python

Classes with `SKLEARN`, `CATEGORY_ENCODERS`, `PYLMNN` or `KERAS` in their name call Python:

| Classes | Python modules needed |
| --- | --- |
| `CLS.SKLEARN.*`, `REG.SKLEARN.*`, `MAP.SKLEARN.*`, `ENC.SKLEARN.OHE`, `BIN.SKLEARN.KMC`, `FET.SKLEARN.MFG`, `TRM.SKLEARN` | `scikit-learn`, `joblib` |
| `CLS.SKLEARN.XGB`, `REG.SKLEARN.XGB` | `xgboost` |
| `ENC.CATEGORY_ENCODERS.*` | `category_encoders` |
| `MAP.PYLMNN.LMNN` | `pylmnn` |
| `CLS.KERAS.DNN` | `tensorflow` (through the R packages keras and tensorflow) |
| Row sampling with `smp.method = 'smote'` | `smote_variants` |

All other classes are pure R and need no Python.

### "No module named 'sklearn'" although sklearn is installed

```
> lr = CLS.SKLEARN.LR(name = 'lr')
Error in py_module_import(module, convert = convert) :
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sklearn'
```

reticulate is using a different Python from the one you installed sklearn into. A computer often has
several: one from python.org, one from conda, one from the Microsoft Store, and one that reticulate
manages itself. See which one reticulate uses:

```{r}
reticulate::py_config()
```

The first line, `python:`, is the Python in use. If the output ends with
`NOTE: Python version was forced by VIRTUAL_ENV` and the path contains `reticulate/uv`, reticulate is
using its own managed Python, which has none of the packages you installed with `pip`.

Two rules explain most of the confusion:

* **reticulate binds to one Python per R session**, the first time any Python code runs. After that,
  `use_python()` and `RETICULATE_PYTHON` have no effect until you **restart R**. Creating a Python-based
  rml model counts as running Python code, even if it fails.
* **Python and R must have the same architecture.** An x86-64 build of R cannot load an ARM64 Python,
  and the reverse. On Windows on ARM machines the default Python download is often ARM64
  (its folder contains `arm64`, for example `pythoncore-3.15-arm64`), while the default R download is
  x86-64. Check R with `R.version$arch`: `"x86_64"` is the Intel/AMD build, `"aarch64"` the ARM build.

Pick one of the fixes below, then restart R.

### Fix 1 (recommended): let reticulate install the modules

Recent versions of reticulate (1.41 and later) manage a Python environment for you and install the
modules you declare with `py_require()`. It always matches R's architecture.

```{r}
library(rml)
reticulate::py_require(c("scikit-learn", "category_encoders", "joblib"))
lr = CLS.SKLEARN.LR(name = 'lr')
```

`py_require()` must run before the first Python-based model in each session. The first call downloads
the modules; later sessions use a cache. To run it in every session, add the line to your `~/.Rprofile`
(open it with `usethis::edit_r_profile()` or `file.edit("~/.Rprofile")`).

Add any other module you need, for example `"xgboost"` for `CLS.SKLEARN.XGB` or `"pylmnn"` for
`MAP.PYLMNN.LMNN`. Specific versions can be requested as `"scikit-learn>=1.5"`.

### Fix 2: use a Python you installed yourself

1. Install a Python with the same architecture as R. For x86-64 R on Windows, use the "Windows installer
   (64-bit)" from python.org, not the ARM64 one. Versions supported by all modules (currently 3.11 to
   3.13) are the safest choice; the newest Python release often lacks packages for a while.
2. Install the modules with that Python, from a terminal:

   ```
   C:/path/to/python.exe -m pip install scikit-learn category_encoders joblib
   ```

3. Tell reticulate to use it. Either add this line to `~/.Renviron` (open it with
   `usethis::edit_r_environ()` or `file.edit("~/.Renviron")`) and restart R:

   ```
   RETICULATE_PYTHON=C:/path/to/python.exe
   ```

   or call this at the start of the session, before any Python-based model:

   ```{r}
   reticulate::use_python("C:/path/to/python.exe", required = TRUE)
   ```

Use forward slashes (`/`) in Windows paths. A virtualenv or conda environment works the same way with
`reticulate::use_virtualenv("name")` or `reticulate::use_condaenv("name")`.

### Fix 3: choose Python from the model

Every Python-based class accepts `python_address`:

```{r}
lr = CLS.SKLEARN.LR(name = 'lr', python_address = "C:/path/to/python.exe")
```

This only works for the first Python-based model of the session (see the rule above), so fixes 1 and
2 are more reliable.

### Checking the setup

```{r}
reticulate::py_config()                          # Python in use, should be the one you chose
reticulate::py_module_available("sklearn")       # TRUE
reticulate::py_module_available("category_encoders")
R.version$arch                                   # architecture of R
```

### Other Python errors

| Message | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Python shared library not found` or `failed to load` | The Python's architecture differs from R's, or it is a Microsoft Store Python. Use fix 1 or a python.org Python of the right architecture. |
| `numpy.core.multiarray failed to import`, or errors mentioning numpy 2 | An old reticulate with numpy 2. Update reticulate (`install.packages("reticulate")`). |
| `InvalidParameterError: The 'max_iter' parameter ... must be an int ... Got 100.0` | R numbers are doubles. rml (from version 1.5.0) sends whole numbers as Python integers; with an older rml write `max_iter = 100L`. An argument passed as a list or inside another object is not converted, so use `L` there. |
| `class should be either a character-string name or a class definition` when creating a model | An argument named `C` (or another prefix of `Class`, such as `Cl`) is matched to the `Class` argument of R's `new()`. Pass it inside `config`: `CLS.SKLEARN.SVM(config = list(C = 0.5))`. |
| `ConvergenceWarning: lbfgs failed to converge` | A warning, not an error: the model is fitted but may not be optimal. Scale the features (`transformers = list(MAP.RML.ZFS())`) or raise `max_iter`. `CLS.SKLEARN.LR` uses `max_iter = 1000` by default. |
| A fitted Python model gives errors after `model_load()` | Python objects are saved with joblib next to the RDS file. Keep the whole folder written by `model_save()` and load it with `model_load()`, not `readRDS()`. |
| Parallel fitting (`mc.num_cores > 1`) fails for Python models | Each worker starts its own R and Python. rml must be installed (not only sourced), and the Python setup must apply to every session, so use `~/.Rprofile` or `~/.Renviron` (fixes 1 and 2) rather than a call in your script. |

## R packages

### Optional packages

Only the packages rml needs everywhere are installed with it. Classes that wrap another package need
that package installed; an error such as `there is no package called 'xgboost'` means it is missing:

| Classes or features | Package |
| --- | --- |
| `CLS.XGBOOST`, `REG.XGBOOST` | xgboost |
| `CLS.KERAS.DNN` | keras, tensorflow |
| `CLS.E1071.NB` | e1071 |
| `CLS.MLR` | mlr |
| `CLS.HDPENREG.FLASSO` | HDPenReg |
| `CLS.SPARKLYR.GBT`, `spark.*` functions | sparklyr |
| `ENC.FASTDUMMIES.OHE` | fastDummies |
| `BIN.SMBINNING.OB` | smbinning |
| `service_models()`, `hp_booster()`, `evaluate_features()` | purrr |
| `mc.num_cores > 1` | doParallel |
| WIDETABLE inputs | rwidetable (or the older rbig) |

The genpack packages (rutils, rwidetable, rvis) are installed from GitHub:

```{r}
remotes::install_github("genpack/rutils")
remotes::install_github("genpack/rml")
```

### xgboost versions

rml works with both the xgboost 1.x and 3.x R packages and translates the arguments that were renamed
between them (`watchlist`/`evals`, `obj`/`objective`, `feval`/`custom_metric`). Other arguments rml
does not use itself are passed to xgboost unchanged, so use the names of the xgboost parameter
documentation.

## Model errors

| Message | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Model not fitted!` | `predict()` was called before `fit()`, or fitting failed. For a transformer, the error is kept in `transformer$objects$fitting_error`. |
| `Model ... does not support gradient transformers yet` | Only `CLS.XGBOOST`, `CLS.STATS.LR` and `CLS.KERAS.DNN` (and every regressor) can be boosted. See `vignette('rml-gradient-boosting')`. |
| `SMOTE sampling cannot be used with gradient transformers` | Synthetic rows have no gradient. Use `smp.method = 'upsample'` or `'downsample'`. |
| `No features left for training the model!` | Column filters (`column_filters`, which by default drop constant columns) or the feature selection removed every column. Check `features.include`, `features.exclude` and `column_filters`. |
| `Features ... were not generated by transformers! Filled with zero.` | The data given to `predict()` lacks columns the model was trained on. Pass the same columns as in training. |
| A transformer is silently missing from the model | It failed to fit and was removed (`remove_failed_transformers = TRUE`). Look at its `objects$fitting_error`. |
| `could not find function` inside a class you wrote | Methods of your class run in your environment. Load rml with `library(rml)` before defining the class. |

## Getting help

Every class and function has a help page (`?CLS.XGBOOST`, `?MODEL`, `?python_setup`). When reporting a
problem, include the output of `sessionInfo()`, and for Python-based models also
`reticulate::py_config()`.
